worldview.title: 1 · Worldview
worldview.intro: Three paths: A real-world backdrop (only write custom deviations), B small world (iterate complete), C big world (split into a constant core plus triggered detail). Constant entries burn tokens in every prompt; triggered ones light up on keywords.
worldview.placeholder: Path C. A harbor town under thirty years of fog; bells carry news; the lighthouse lights only half its lamp (keeper secret)…
worldview.q1: Which path fits this card: A real backdrop, B small world, or C big world?
worldview.q2: What is ALWAYS true here that a model would guess wrong? (that is your constant core)
worldview.q3: Which places, factions or names deserve their own triggered entry, under which keywords?

basics.title: 2 · Character basics
basics.intro: The differentiation principle: write ONLY what deviates from the model's default assumption. “A Japanese girl with black hair” says nothing — blonde dye, a scar, a wrong accent make the cut.
basics.placeholder: Ali, deckhand, 24. Scar from left brow to cheekbone — her smile pulls sideways. Speaks in dock shorthand…
basics.q1: Name, rough age, occupation or identity?
basics.q2: Which traits DEVIATE from what a model would assume by default? Only those are worth ink.
basics.q3: What would a stranger notice within three seconds (scar, gait, accent, habit)?
basics.q4: Which single background fact drives how they act today?

palette.title: 3 · Personality palette
palette.intro: A base coat under everything, 1-2 main colors people actually see, one accent as seasoning. Every main color needs handwritten derivation loops — scene → behavior → spoken line. Illogical-but-alive combinations are what only a person can write.
palette.placeholder: Base: inferiority (never speaks first). Main: competitive (loses, then drills all night claiming it's “just exercise”)…
palette.q1: The base coat — the trait lying under everything?
palette.q2: The 1-2 main colors people actually see day to day?
palette.q3: One small accent trait as seasoning?
palette.q4: For EACH main color, handwrite derivation loops: a concrete scene → what they do → one spoken line.

facets.title: 4 · Three facets (optional)
facets.intro: Gears of ONE engine, not three personalities. Each facet = trigger + energy + voice + body + function, and the other facets bleed through it. Skip this for simple characters.
facets.placeholder: Day-shift deckhand (strangers present): short sentences, hands never idle. Night watcher (alone on the pier): …
facets.q1: What flips the character between facets — place, audience, threat?
facets.q2: For each facet: what energy runs it, and what does the voice sound like (give a sample line)?
facets.q3: What does each facet DO for them — its function?
facets.q4: How do the other facets bleed through each one?

exegesis.title: 5 · Second exegesis
exegesis.intro: The author's final margin notes — what stops the model from completing your character out of its own training data. Entirely handwritten; the AI may only ask you questions.
exegesis.placeholder: She is NOT a tsundere template: her sharp tongue targets only the strong; with the weak she is plainly direct. Never write her blushing.
exegesis.q1: What is this character NOT — which obvious reading is wrong?
exegesis.q2: What would a model wrongly auto-complete from its stock tropes?
exegesis.q3: What stays fixed no matter where the story goes?

wardrobe.title: 6 · Wardrobe & carried items
wardrobe.intro: Triggered-layer entries keyed on outfit words and the character's name. Every item should hold a story — a lighter that no longer lights beats a catalog of clothes.
wardrobe.placeholder: Work jacket, cuffs frayed, a knife sheath sewn into the left pocket. Carries her mother's cracked compass…
wardrobe.q1: Daily outfit — and the one detail that is off or wrong about it?
wardrobe.q2: What do they always carry, and what story does each item hold?
wardrobe.q3: Which keywords should trigger these entries?

nsfw.title: 7 · NSFW palette (optional)
nsfw.intro: Write the WHY, not the WHAT: drives, dynamics and boundaries as personality facts. The core motivation is handwritten-only. Entries land keeper-only. What you write is organized faithfully — no watering down.
nsfw.placeholder: Intimacy is the only way she ever goes off-watch — that is the why…
nsfw.q1: WHY does intimacy matter to this character — what does it mean to them? (handwritten)
nsfw.q2: Which dynamics and preferences follow from their personality, stated as facts?

npcs.title: 8 · NPCs
npcs.intro: One triggered entry per NPC, keyed on the name. One concrete, memorable detail each — an NPC exists to be recognized, not summarized.
npcs.placeholder: Old Chen, foreman, owes her his life and keeps trying to repay it in fish…
npcs.q1: Who orbits this character — two to four people at most?
npcs.q2: One concrete distinguishing detail per NPC?
npcs.q3: Which keywords trigger each entry (usually the name)?

overview.title: 9 · Quick reference
overview.intro: The always-on index card: 8-15 terse lines the model must never lose sight of. It rides in every prompt — every line must earn its tokens.
overview.placeholder: Ali / deckhand / scar brow→cheek / base: inferiority, main: competitive / investigating the lighthouse night…
overview.q1: Which 8-15 lines must the model never lose sight of?
overview.q2: What is the current situation as the story opens?

opening.title: 10 · Opening message
opening.intro: The opening sets the register the model will imitate. Place the player, give the character one concrete action and real dialogue, end on a hook. The anti-pattern lint applies at full force.
opening.placeholder: The bell struck four. Ali looped the mooring line without looking up: “You're standing where a man died last night.”
opening.q1: Where does the scene open, and what is the character DOING?
opening.q2: What is their first spoken line?
opening.q3: What hook can the player immediately act on?

variables.title: 11 · Variables & state
variables.intro: Loreweaver-native closing stage: [InitVar] YAML for initial state — scalar leaves auto-promote to typed, validated variables — plus plain-language update rules that land as a hooks draft.
variables.placeholder: Trust 0..10 starting 0; lighthouse clues 0..5; has-seen-the-fog flag…
variables.q1: Which state does the STORY actually read back — meters, stages, flags?
variables.q2: Ranges and starting values for each?
variables.q3: When does each variable move, and by how much (one rule per line)?

err.packPresentationPaletteCount: Presentation kit: at most {{max}} palette entries.
err.packPresentationPaletteTooLong: Presentation kit: palette entry {{index}} is longer than {{max}} characters.
err.packItemNeedsBytes: “{{file}}” is missing its file contents — re-attach it on the Classify step before building.
err.rulepackAlias: Rulepack: YAML anchors/aliases are refused by the engine's loader rather than expanded — write the value out.
err.rulepackNotMapping: Rulepack: the YAML root must be a mapping of sections.
err.rulepackUnknownSection: Rulepack: “{{section}}” is not a section the engine reads, so it will be silently ignored — check the spelling.
err.rulepackExtendsType: Rulepack: `extends:` must be the id of one system to patch.
err.rulepackDefaultScalar: Rulepack: the default for “{{stat}}” must be a single value.
err.rulepackAliasList: Rulepack: aliases for “{{stat}}” must be a list of names.
err.rulepackDerivedMapping: Rulepack: the derived spec for “{{stat}}” must be a mapping.
err.rulepackDerivedOp: Rulepack: the derived spec for “{{stat}}” names no operation. One of: {{ops}}.
err.rulepackDerivedComputer: Rulepack: “{{stat}}” uses `{{op}}:`, which resolves only where the operator registered code at startup — the engine ships that registry empty, so this pack will not load on a stock server.
err.rulepackDerivedExprKeys: Rulepack: the expr spec for “{{stat}}” has unknown key(s) {{keys}} — only `expr` and `format` are read.
err.rulepackDerivedExprText: Rulepack: the expr for “{{stat}}” must be a non-empty string.
err.rulepackDerivedUnknownStat: Rulepack: “{{stat}}” derives from “{{of}}”, which this pack never declares — the engine will read it as 0.
err.rulepackTurnCheckMapping: Rulepack: turn_checks[{{index}}] must be a mapping.
err.rulepackTurnCheckKey: Rulepack: turn_checks[{{index}}] has an unknown key “{{field}}”.
err.rulepackTurnCheckWhen: Rulepack: turn_checks[{{index}}] needs a `when:` condition name.
err.rulepackInitiativeRoll: Rulepack: `initiative:` must be a mapping with a non-empty `roll:` expression — a bare string is refused. Write `initiative:` then an indented `roll: 1d20+DEX`.
err.rulepackScriptBareName: Rulepack: the script name “{{file}}” has a path in it. A rules script sits next to its YAML, so the name must be a bare file name.
err.rulepackScriptMissing: Rulepack: this YAML declares the rules script “{{file}}”, but the pack ships no source for it — the build will fail on the missing file.
err.rulepackScriptOrphan: Rulepack: a rules script is attached, but the YAML names none. Declare it as `resolution.script` or `subsystems.<id>.script`, or the file will not be shipped.
err.rulepackScriptTooLong: Rulepack: the rules script exceeds the sandbox's {{max}}-character cap.
err.rulepackThin: Rulepack: this file neither extends a system nor defines one — nothing in it will change how the table plays.
err.packPrepNotJs: Prep script “{{file}}” must be a .js file — the engine's build rejects any other extension.
err.packPrepPath: Prep script “{{file}}”: use a plain file name; scripts land directly under prep/.
err.packPrepTooLong: Prep script “{{file}}” exceeds the sandbox's {{max}}-character cap.
err.packRulesScriptPath: Rules script “{{file}}”: use a bare file name — the engine reads a script from beside its rulepack YAML and refuses a path.
err.packRulesScriptNotJs: Rules script “{{file}}” must be a .js file.
err.packPresetPath: Preset “{{file}}”: use a plain file name; presets land directly under presets/.
err.packPresetNoId: Preset “{{file}}”: the file name yields no usable store id.
err.packPresetIdCollision: Preset “{{file}}” installs as “{{id}}”, which another preset in this pack already claims — they would overwrite each other in the shared store.
err.packPresetNotObject: Preset “{{file}}”: the root must be a JSON object (a SillyTavern completion preset).
err.packPresetNoPrompts: Preset “{{file}}” has no `prompts` array — this is not a SillyTavern completion preset.
err.packPresetEmptyPrompts: Preset “{{file}}” has an empty `prompts` array — there is no prompt text to fold, so a sampling-only preset cannot ship as a pack asset.
err.packPresetTooManyPrompts: Preset “{{file}}” holds more than {{max}} prompt entries.

panels.hint: Optional: declare ui/panels.yaml (Tier-1 blocks render everywhere; a Tier-2 panel ships HTML/JS/CSS under its own ui/<panel>/ directory and MUST declare a fallback). Files added below land verbatim in the source tree.

skills.title: Hand-written skills
skills.hint: Optional: full SKILL.md documents (frontmatter + prompt sections) with an optional hooks.js — for keeper-style direction skills, not just hook extraction.

presentation.emptyTitle: Presentation kit (演出资料包) — the Stage Director's brief
presentation.emptyHint: The Stage Director stages beats (images, letters, clippings, title cards, audio) only for modules that ship a kit — no kit, no generated staging for this pack's rooms. That gate is the point: a module opts in by saying, once and as data, what it should look and sound like. Adding one is always optional.
presentation.doctrineGated: Kit-gated and knowledge-scoped: the Director reads only this file, the player-visible stream, and exposed state — never keeper material. Everything written here is safe to be inferred from a player's screen.
presentation.doctrineRef: Ref-mandatory (定妆): a subject without a reference image can never be generated — no ref, no portrait. The ref and the style keywords ride every image request, because consistency is the hard part.
presentation.doctrinePackOnly: 宁缺毋滥: you may veto generation outright (pack art only). No config flag overrides an atmosphere-first author.
presentation.doctrineWarmup: 慢菜先备 is the runtime's job, not yours: once a subject is nameable here, the engine can warm its art during idle turns.
presentation.hint: ui/presentation.yaml — one look per module. The engine re-validates everything here at pack build; the issues below are what it would reject, said early.

testDrive.title: Test this pack now
testDrive.hint: Installs the built pack into the local server's own data folder, starts that server (restarting it when the pack ships skills or rulepacks, which are registered at startup), joins as keeper, and issues the pack's import commands. Then it hands you the live table.

testDrive.mountHint: Skips the build entirely: the local server mounts your SOURCE tree and the room follows every save — lore, skills, rulepacks and panels reload live, and the room's variable values survive. A dev mount serves panels and the kit straight from source, past the build-time caps, so keep testing the built pack before you release.

pack.needsBytes: Restored without its bytes: {{name}} ({{size}} bytes). Everything else came back.

rulepack.title: Rule system
rulepack.patchHint: An `extends:` over a system the engine already ships — override a few defaults and leave the rest alone.
rulepack.fullHint: A whole system authored here: stats, derived formulas, resolution, sheet, subsystems, commands. Both modes write the same rulepacks/<id>.yaml; the file stem is the id players type in `.set`.
rulepack.scriptHint: This YAML declares a rules script, so the pack must ship it beside the YAML under exactly that name. The sandbox calls one function — `resolve` for a resolution script, `flow` for a subsystem — and takes its return value; nothing else in the file runs on its own.
rulepack.advisory: Advisory only — the engine parses this file again at build time and its verdict is the one that counts.

prep.title: Prep-phase scripts
prep.hint: Bulk setup a keeper runs once, by reference, in the prep phase: forty NPCs from a list, a family of variables. The script PLANS the work; the engine applies the plan after showing it whole. Nothing here ever runs at install.
prep.apiPlan: plan(tool, args) is the ONLY callable. The sandbox has no engine state, no host and no network — a script emits an operation list and stops.
prep.apiLimits: Limits: {{chars}} characters of script, {{ops}} operations per plan, 8 KB of arguments per operation, 1 s of CPU.
prep.apiGating: Each planned call goes through the same argument validation, keeper_only marking and gated-skill check a model-issued call gets — because it is the same code.
prep.apiUnreachable: `.import … world` and `.var expose` are keeper COMMANDS, not tools, so a plan can never name them.
prep.apiPreview: Preview is free: the keeper runs it with apply off, reads the whole operation list, and only then applies.
prep.readingLoop: a loop plans an unknown number — the engine caps a plan at {{ops}} operations
prep.forbidden: This script names {{names}}, which the sandbox does not expose. It will fail at preview.
prep.invoke: The keeper runs it with: run_prep_plan(script_ref="{{ref}}")

episodes.title: Episodes (serialized module)
episodes.hint: One pack, cumulative versions: the release at episode N contains episodes 1..N and nothing of N+1. That is what makes the file you circulate spoiler-safe — there is no gating machinery, because there is nothing later inside it. Add episodes here, tag files on the Classify step, and pick the release checkpoint on Build.
episodes.releaseNotesPlaceholder: What a reader who already played the previous installment needs to know.
episodes.buildUpToHint: Episodes 1–{{n}} ship; anything tagged later is left out of the source tree entirely.
episodes.versionHint: The convention is MINOR = episode, so this build would be {{suggested}} rather than {{version}}.

pack.installTargetHint: Every install here lands in {{dir}} — the local server's own data folder, so the pack you just built is the one it will serve. The command above carries the same override, so pasting it does what the button does.

presets.title: Prompt presets
presets.hint: Ship a keeper style with the module. Install lands each preset in the server's SHARED preset store — install is not enable, so nothing turns on by itself: a keeper folds one into a room with `.preset enable <id>`. What ships is the document as you imported it, not the preview toggles.

lint.title: Advisory lint
lint.hint: Advisory only — the engine build stays the authority. These are the things that build fine and then do nothing.

msg.variableUnused: Variable “{{id}}” is declared but never mentioned by any lore entry, panel or hook.
msg.loreNeverActivates: Lore entry “{{title}}” can never activate: no keys, not constant, no condition.
msg.bilingualGapVariable: Variable “{{id}}” has a label in one language only (missing: {{missing}}).
msg.bilingualGapPanel: Panel “{{panel}}”: the {{field}} text is in one language only (missing: {{missing}}).
msg.bilingualGapPack: The pack {{field}} is in one language only (missing: {{missing}}).
msg.panelBindsHiddenVariable: Panel “{{panel}}” binds the keeper-only variable “{{id}}”: hidden variables never reach a player's client, so the block renders blank for them.
msg.panelConditionHiddenVariable: Panel “{{panel}}” gates a block on the keeper-only variable “{{id}}”: the condition never decides true for a player, and the condition string ships with the pack, so the variable's name leaks.
msg.panelBindsUnknownVariable: Panel “{{panel}}” binds “{{id}}”, which this pack never declares.
msg.codeUnknownVariable: {{origin}} reads or writes “{{id}}”, which this pack never declares.
msg.loreUnknownVariable: Lore entry “{{title}}” names “{{id}}”, which this pack never declares.
msg.stubMarker: {{origin}} still carries the wizard's draft stub, so the update rules never run.
msg.packDescriptionMissing: The pack has no description in either language — it is what a reader sees before installing.
msg.assetMissing: {{from}} points at “{{path}}”, which this pack does not ship.
msg.episodeUnknown: Lore entry “{{title}}” is tagged to episode “{{tag}}”, which this pack does not declare. It will still ship — a typo must not silently cut your work — but it is in every release, not the one you meant.
msg.episodeNoNotes: Episode {{ordinal}} (“{{title}}”) will ship with no release notes, so its CHANGELOG entry says nothing about what changed.
msg.episodeForwardReference: Lore entry “{{title}}” (episode {{ordinal}}) names “{{name}}”, which episode {{ahead}} introduces. In the release that ships episode {{ordinal}}, that reference has nothing behind it.

exportFlavor.label: ST card flavor
exportFlavor.safeHint: {{n}} keeper-only entr(ies) will be STRIPPED. Everything in a SillyTavern card is player-visible, so this is the card you can hand out.
exportFlavor.releaseHint: {{n}} keeper-only entr(ies) will be KEPT. A SillyTavern card has no hidden half — anyone who opens this file reads them.

importErr.notAnObject: “{{file}}” is not a card: a SillyTavern card is a JSON object (v2/v3 wrap their fields in `data`), and this file's top level is something else.
importErr.unsupportedFormat: “{{file}}” could not be read as a card. Expected SillyTavern JSON (v2/v3), a Loreweaver native bundle (*.lorecard.json), or a PNG with an embedded card — the bytes are none of those.
importErr.notJson: “{{file}}” is not valid JSON, so nothing could be read out of it. If it came from a PNG export, drop the .png itself.
importErr.notALorecard: “{{file}}” is JSON, but not a Loreweaver native bundle: the `format: loreweaver.card` tag is missing. A SillyTavern card goes through the card splitter instead.
importErr.unsupportedLorecardVersion: “{{file}}” declares native-bundle format_version {{detail}}; this studio reads v1.
importErr.pngWithoutCard: “{{file}}” is a valid PNG but carries no embedded card: the `chara` / `ccv3` text chunk that holds one is absent. It was probably saved by an image editor, which drops those chunks.
importErr.invalidEmbeddedPayload: “{{file}}” carries an embedded card chunk, but its payload is not readable base64 JSON — the chunk is corrupt or was written by an incompatible tool.
importErr.decompressTooLarge: “{{file}}” expands to more than this studio will decompress. A card that large is either corrupt or hostile.
importErr.fileTooLarge: “{{file}}” is larger than the card size cap.

initvar.syntax: “{{where}}”: the [InitVar] block does not parse — {{detail}} No variables were taken from it.
initvar.notAMapping: “{{where}}”: the [InitVar] block parsed, but its top level is not a mapping of variables. No variables were taken from it.
initvar.alias: “{{where}}”: the [InitVar] block uses YAML anchors/aliases, which are refused rather than expanded. No variables were taken from it.
initvar.syntaxAt: “{{where}}”: the [InitVar] block does not parse at line {{line}} — {{detail}} No variables were taken from it.

studio.macroDeterminism: {{random}} / {{pick}} (and a lore entry's probability roll) are seeded per room and TURN: different turns vary freely, but re-running the same turn — a retry, an undo replay — reproduces the same picks. Expect “random” to repeat within one turn; that is what makes a turn reconstructable. The two draws use separate streams, so adding a {{random}} never shifts which probabilistic entries fire.
